prompt:
A densely annotated editorial infographic plate, drawn by hand in confident ink
line with light watercolour and gouache wash on bright warm-white paper.
Contour line varies in weight and is charcoal near-black. Dimensional but not
photographic: restrained hatching, subtle texture, believable volume, selective
shadow, clean uncluttered background. Every material reads as itself — dull grey
lead, unglazed earthenware, weathered timber, damp fibrous bark — and materials
that differ in the explanation look visibly different. Quiet palette of stone,
clay, wood, and metal tones over the warm-white ground, with one or two
desaturated accents that each keep a single meaning throughout the plate.
Contemporary editorial typography: one calm display face for the title, one
highly legible face for the many small labels, sentence case, crisply printed
and correctly spelled. Annotation is dense and disciplined — leader lines,
brackets, dimension marks, magnified inset circles, small side studies — laid
out so no two leaders cross. Asymmetric composition with about a quarter of the
page left quiet. Modern printing on clean stock: fresh, crisp, and unaged. The
only lettering anywhere on the plate is the title, the deck, the labels, and the
short notes. The words hero, drawing, figure, plate, inset, zone, band, strip,
trio, column, and cutaway describe the construction of the page and are never
lettered onto it, alone or in a phrase: no headings that name parts of the
layout, no percentages or
proportions of the page, no tags in brackets after a label or note, no sentence
describing the drawing or explaining what the reader is meant to see, no
signature, monogram, date, watermark, or credit line.

The plate is headed "image", with the standing line "Turns a pair of prompts into one PNG, refusing unsupported models before any paid request and logging every response in a ledger." beneath it.

The dominant picture, filling roughly half the page, shows Two paper sheets, technical prompt and enhanced prompt, merge into one final prompt sheet. That sheet passes the image model tag, gpt-image-2 by default. A key drawn from the creds box joins it, chosen by the model's provider. Together they pass a registry checkpoint gate. The path then forks into two provider branches, OpenAI and Gemini. Image bytes flow back from both and rejoin at a single .png file dropping into the generated folder. From there the file continues onward toward annotation. A thin side arrow leaves the provider response and runs to a ledger book.

Magnified circles set beside it show The first circle shows JPEG bytes from Gemini entering and a PNG leaving, which is re-encoding rather than relabelling. The second circle shows an unsupported legacy model stopped at the gate before any request is sent. The third circle shows a missing key producing an empty placeholder file and no API call. The frames show landscape, portrait and square. OpenAI receives these as pixel sizes and Gemini as aspect ratios.

Colour is used so that Warm ochre marks the prompt and image data path. Red marks refusal and stop points. Blue-green marks ledger accounting.

Draw these quantities as dimension marks or counts: 2 prompts joined into 1 final prompt. 2 providers, OpenAI and Gemini. 3 aspect ratios, 3:2, 2:3 and 1:1. 2 output folders, generated and annotated. 3 progress phases. 1 ledger row per parsed response.

These trade words appear on the plate, each set against the thing it names: technical prompt and enhanced prompt sit on the two incoming sheets. gpt-image-2 sits on the model tag. creds sits on the key box. The registry check sits at the gate. image_wait sits in the first timeline phase and image_download in the second. annotate sits in the third phase and on the caption step. terse prompt sits on the caption at the image's bottom edge. generated and annotated sit on the two folders. .png sits on both finished files. The ledger row sits in the accounting book.

Letter these words onto the drawings, spelled exactly as given: technical prompt, enhanced prompt, final prompt, image model, gpt-image-2, creds, API key, registry check, OpenAI, Gemini JPEG in, PNG out, unsupported model, no paid request, empty placeholder landscape, portrait, square, pixel size, aspect ratio generated, annotated, terse prompt, ledger row, .png image_wait, image_download, annotate

Set these short notes beside what they explain: Two prompts join into one; Key chosen by the model's provider Legacy models refused before any paid request; No key: empty file, no API call OpenAI takes pixels, Gemini takes ratios Caption set along the bottom edge; Each parsed response records one ledger row; Ledger failures never discard an image Download phase begins only when reported
